entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Ps.95.1-Ps.95.2">Psa 95:1-2</reference> <div eID="gen9937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9938" type="x-p"/> Jahve is called the Rock of our salvation (as in <reference osisRef="Ps.89.27">Psa 89:27</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Ps.94.22">Psa 94:22</reference>) as being its firm and sure ground. Visiting the house of God, one comes before God’s face; קדּם פּני, <hi type="italic">praeoccupare faciem</hi>, is equivalent to <hi type="italic">visere </hi>(<hi type="italic">visitare</hi>). תּודה is not <hi type="italic">confessio peccati</hi>, but <hi type="italic">laudis</hi>. The <hi type="italic">Beth</hi> before תודה is the <hi type="italic">Beth</hi> of accompaniment, as in Mic 6:6; that before זמרות (according to <reference osisRef="2Sam.23.1">2Sa 23:1</reference> a name for psalms, whilst מזמר can only be used as a technical expression) is the <hi type="italic">Beth</hi> of the medium.

Visiting the house of God, one comes before God’s face; קדּם פּני, praeoccupare faciem , is equivalent to visere ( visitare ). תּודה is not confessio peccati , but laudis . entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Ps.95.3-Ps.95.7">Psa 95:3-7</reference> <div eID="gen9938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9939" type="x-p"/> The adorableness of God receives a threefold confirmation: He is exalted above all gods as King, above all things as Creator, and above His people as Shepherd and Leader. אלהים (gods) here, as in Psa 96:4., <reference osisRef="Ps.97.7">Psa 97:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.97.9">Psa 97:9</reference>, and frequently, are the powers of the natural world and of the world of men, which the Gentiles deify and call kings (as Moloch Molech, the deified fire), which, however, all stand under the lordship of Jahve, who is infinitely exalted above everything that is otherwise called god (<reference osisRef="Ps.96.4">Psa 96:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.97.9">Psa 97:9</reference>). The supposition that תּועפות הרים denotes the pit-works (μέταλλα) of the mountains (Böttcher), is at once improbable, because to all appearance it is intended to be the antithesis to מחקרי־ארץ, the shafts of the earth. The derivation from ועף (יעף), κάμνειν, κοπιᾶν, also does not suit תועפות in Num 23:22; Num 24:8, for “fatigues” and “indefatigableness” are notions that lie very wide apart. The כּסף תּועפות of <reference osisRef="Job.22.25">Job 22:25</reference> might more readily be explained according to this “silver of fatigues,” i.e., silver that the fatiguing labour of mining brings to light, and תועפות הרים in the passage before us, with Gussetius, Geier, and Hengstenberg: <hi type="italic">cacumina montium quia defatigantur qui eo ascendunt</hi>, prop. ascendings = summits of the mountains, after which כסף תועפות, <reference osisRef="Job.22.25">Job 22:25</reference>, might also signify “silver of the mountain-heights.” But the lxx, which renders δόξα in the passages in Numbers and τὰ ὕψη τῶν ὀρέων in the passage before us, leads one to a more correct track. The verb יעף (ועף), transposed from יפע (ופע), goes back to the root יף, וף, to stand forth, tower above, to be high, according to which תועפות = תופעות signifies <hi type="italic">eminentiae</hi>, i.e., towerings = summits, or prominences = high (the highest) perfection (vid., on <reference osisRef="Job.22.25">Job 22:25</reference>). In the passage before us it is a synonym of the Arabic <hi type="italic">mı̂fan , mı̂fâtun , pars terrae eminens</hi> (from Arab. <hi type="italic">wfâ</hi> = יפע, prop. instrumentally: a means of rising above, viz., by climbing), and of the names of eminences derived from Arab. <hi type="italic">yf'</hi> (after which Hitzig renders: the teeth of the mountains). By reason of the fact that Jahve is the Owner (cf. <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.8">1Sa 2:8</reference>), because the Creator of all things, the call to worship, which concerns no one so nearly as it does Israel, the people, which before other peoples is Jahve’s creation, viz., the creation of His miraculously mighty grace, is repeated. In the call or invitation, השׁתּחוה signifies to stretch one’s self out full length upon the ground, the proper attitude of adoration; כּרע, to curtsey, to totter; and בּרך, Arabic <hi type="italic">baraka</hi>, starting from the radical signification <hi type="italic">flectere</hi>, to kneel down, <hi type="italic">in genua</hi> (πρόχνυ, <hi type="italic">pronum</hi> = <hi type="italic">procnum</hi>) <hi type="italic">procumbere</hi>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.6.13">2Ch 6:13</reference> (cf. Hölemann, <hi type="italic">Bibelstudien</hi>, i. 135f.). Beside עם מרעיתו, people of His pasture, צאן ידו is not the flock formed by His creating hand (Augustine: <hi type="italic">ipse gratiâ suâ nos oves fecit</hi>), but, after <reference osisRef="Gen.30.35">Gen 30:35</reference>, the flock under His protection, the flock led and defended by His skilful, powerful hand. Böttcher renders: flock of His charge; but יד in this sense (<reference osisRef="Jer.6.3">Jer 6:3</reference>) signifies only a place, and “flock of His place” would be poetry and prose in one figure.
